1.explanation: Both of these files render <button> elements purely as part of the skeleton UI without any visible text or programmatic label (aria-label or aria-labelledby). Because DAP requires every form control to have an associated label, these two skeleton-specific components must be updated—either by adding an aria-label prop or by including hidden text—to satisfy the accessibility rule.
1.bug_scenario: When running the IBM DAP accessibility checker on the React “Accordion Skeleton” and “Button Skeleton” components, every generated <button> element in those skeleton UIs is flagged as missing an associated label (no text or aria-label/aria-labelledby). The screenshots show multiple <button type="button" class="bx--accordion__heading"> elements being reported as unlabeled form controls.

2.explanation: Both of these files generate <button> elements in their skeleton UIs without any inner text or an aria-label attribute. Because buttons are form controls, they must have an accessible name or associated <label>. These unlabeled buttons are exactly what the DAP tool is flagging, so these two skeleton files must be updated (for example, by adding aria-label or hiding them from assistive technologies) to resolve the violation.
2.bug_scenario: When running the IBM DAP accessibility analyzer against the React “Skeleton” variants of Accordion and Button, each of the placeholder components renders an actual <button> element without any visible text or aria-label. In the Accordion skeleton, the collapsed/expanded headings are generated as bare button elements; in the Button skeleton, the placeholder button is likewise a <button> with no accessible name. This triggers the rule “Each form control element must have an associated label.”
